A: The chart plots 2025 while the source says the newest period is excluded because of ingest lag; calling that endpoint censored is inconsistent with the plotted data.
The comparison asserts a study comparison group, but the recorded statistic supplies no baseline value.
The effect-estimate CSV says source call research.statistics#1, but the recorded c3 result does not provide the stated comparison-group data.
B: The 2023 child-poverty point and several trial effect sizes are memory estimates, not checkable against the supplied record.
The work comparison combines participation, employment, part-time work, and full-time employment across different studies as a single percentage-point spread.
The export’s Alaska employment null is described as approximately zero despite no numeric value or recorded response establishing that estimate.
C: The record’s qualifying document says poverty reduction increases with benefit generosity in both countries, but the deliverable presents this as a verified conditional poverty reduction finding without the underlying poverty estimates.
The 355 readable-paper count is described as papers carrying a real abstract, omitting that they are title-anchored.
The $11,400 model-based finding is included as a specific claim, though the record marks its document ungrounded and unread.
D: The chart’s historical employment values are not present in the supplied reference record and are presented as measured.
The Alaska DOI 10.1257/pol.20170044 does not resolve to the cited work according to the script check.
The quoted 2024 NBER passage is corrupted (“4. ಕಟ್ಟ”), and the reference does not provide a resolvable DOI or verified quote.

raw.verdict: A is the strongest decision aid: it gives a clear, restrained answer, uses a traceable hardship estimate, and explains why that estimate cannot settle the combined poverty-and-work question. C has stronger research-series and drill-down coverage, but its broad-corpus framing and ungrounded model claim blur what the evidence actually establishes; B and D rely on unverified memory figures.
